title: Amazon tells engineers that token counts are a flawed target, DeepMind’s Genie 4 adds sound and live steering to simulated worlds, and TrendAI finds a 44-agent pen-test tool probing organisations in Japan. Nvidia and AMD are putting $4 billion into Meta’s AI share sale, a report says the UK Home Office is embedding AI in near-total secrecy, Anthropic says its refutation of a core computing conjecture does nothing for real formulas, and Apple is adding assistants to Pages, Keynote and Numbers.
summary: On 27 October 2026 Amazon published a memo telling engineers not to treat token use or lines of code as the target for AI. Google DeepMind released Genie 4, a research-preview world model with native audio and live text steering. TrendAI’s English report described an open-source tool, CyberStrikeAI, running 44 agents against at least 19 organisations, mostly in Japan, with few deep compromises. Nvidia said it would invest $3 billion in Meta’s share sale and AMD $1 billion, $4 billion in total, after Meta’s $95 billion plan. The Guardian reported an Open Rights Group study of AI across the UK Home Office. Anthropic published a proof that the Exponential Time Hypothesis is false and said it does not help solve real formulas. Apple said Creator Studio subscribers will get AI assistants in Pages, Keynote and Numbers in November.
uncertainty: Amazon’s memo text is on its site; CNBC dates the public posting to 27 October and the internal circulation to September, and the May leaderboard shutdown and the lack of a token cap come from CNBC, not the memo. Genie 4’s limits are DeepMind’s own; it is not generally available. TrendAI’s counts are lower bounds from files on attacker servers; the Japanese article was 23 October and the English report 27 October; Case C’s AI use is inferred from writing style. Nvidia’s $3 billion and AMD’s $1 billion are what the companies announced, as CNBC reports; Broadcom’s share of the earlier “up to $5 billion” interest was not stated on Tuesday. The Home Office account is the Open Rights Group’s, via The Guardian; the department says staff still make asylum decisions. Anthropic’s ETH paper is its own claim, published 27 October, and says nothing about practical solving; OpenAI’s related claim, posted 26 October, is still with outside examiners. Apple’s assistants are a November beta for Creator Studio subscribers, in US English, on Apple Intelligence devices.

stories.theme: Amazon tells engineers that token counts and lines of code are a flawed way to score AI use
stories.changed: On Tuesday 27 October 2026 Amazon published a revised role guideline for its software engineers, a memo CNBC says had circulated internally in September. Written by Terk Terkowitz, a vice president and distinguished engineer, it says the outcomes that matter are unchanged: impact on customers, the business and the team. It says input metrics such as token usage, adoption of AI tools, and code changes and reviews are deeply flawed as targets because they are disconnected from what matters. Used as a target, they drive higher cost, which the memo calls tokenmaxxing and says is at odds with frugality, and more complexity, because measuring lines of code is at odds with keeping things simple. The memo still says those metrics can be used with care and judgement, and tells leaders to look at the 10th percentile of AI adoption, teams that are not using it, and the 90th, teams using it heavily, and ask whether delivery has risen to match. It says if your work does not benefit from current AI tools, that is a finding, not a failing. CNBC reports that a spokesperson said Amazon has not capped token use, and that in May the company shut an internal leaderboard after staff used AI heavily to climb it. Marc Brooker, an AWS vice president, told CNBC the company looks at feature velocity: how many launches, and how many successful changes reach production.
stories.matters: Many companies have started scoring teams on how much AI they consume. Amazon, one of the largest, is now saying that score can reward waste.
stories.imply: If your dashboard ranks people by tokens or lines generated, it is measuring the wrong thing. Keep the usage data, and judge the work.
uses: Stop using token totals or lines of AI-written code as a target in performance reviews.
For teams at the heavy end of AI use, check whether launches and successful production changes actually rose.
Let someone record where AI does not help their work, and treat that as useful information.
stories.example: An engineering director retires a weekly token leaderboard. She keeps the usage report for cost, and in reviews asks each team what shipped and where the assistant got in the way.
stories.audience: Engineering managers, HR and finance teams who are scoring AI adoption, and the people being scored.
stories.watch: Whether Amazon’s next guideline names a replacement metric. Whether other large employers drop token targets. What happens to its AI bill.

source.title: Amazon: An update from Amazon engineering leadership on the role of the developer in the age of AI, posted 27 October 2026
source.quote: If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing

stories.theme: DeepMind’s Genie 4 simulates a scene you can steer, with native sound, and it is still a research preview
stories.changed: On Tuesday 27 October 2026 Google DeepMind announced Genie 4, a world model for real-time interactive simulation. It is the lab’s first real-time world model to generate audio natively: ambient sound, music and dialogue, produced with the picture. A person can change a running scene with text, such as the weather, the camera, or a new person or object, and Gemini adapts the prompt to the scene. Gemini 3.8 Flash sits in the loop as a guiding agent, breaking a goal into steps and checking frames. DeepMind has also tried pairing it with Gemini 4 Argon for robotics research, including a simulated humanoid playing checkers. Genie 4 is rolling out as a research preview to trusted testers, then to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and to early-access partners of the Gemini API and Google AI Studio. Every video and audio clip carries SynthID, Google’s watermark. DeepMind says it is early: visual detail and object permanence can drift as a session runs longer, after complex edits, or as you move through a scene. Legible text, audio accuracy and long-term consistency are still open problems.
stories.matters: Teams that storyboard, prototype a game or rehearse a robot task may get a steerable scene instead of a still. It is not a finished shot, and you cannot have it yet unless you are on the tester list.
stories.imply: Treat Genie 4 as a draft of a place, not a record of one. Check anything that has to stay put, including text, and expect a wait for access and a price.
uses: If you storyboard or pre-visualise, join the Project Genie waitlist and try one scene you already know well.
Do not use a Genie clip as evidence of a real place or event. It cannot reproduce real locations accurately, and it is watermarked.
Robotics and game teams: use it to sketch a scenario, then test the same task in your own simulator.
stories.example: A studio’s previz lead asks Genie 4 for a street scene and steers the camera with text. She exports the clip for a meeting, notes that a shop sign smeared as the shot ran on, and still builds the real set in her usual tools.
stories.audience: Film and game teams, robotics groups, and anyone asked to approve synthetic footage.
stories.watch: When it leaves the tester list, and what it costs. Independent checks of how long a scene stays coherent. Whether rivals ship a steerable world model.

source.title: Google DeepMind: Genie 4: A new generation of world simulation, 27 October 2026
source.quote: Genie 4 is our first real-time world model to generate audio natively.

stories.theme: TrendAI found a 44-agent pen-test tool validating at least 19 organisations, mostly in Japan, with few deep break-ins
stories.changed: On 27 October 2026 TrendAI published the English edition of a report first issued in Japanese on 23 October. It analysed three attack setups aimed mainly at Japan, reconstructed from files the attackers left on their own servers, not from victim logs. In the clearest case, an exposed console was running CyberStrikeAI, an open-source penetration-testing tool. A log line, “credential-search agent 8/44”, showed 44 agents splitting the work: reconnaissance, vulnerability checks, exploitation, command and control, persistence, data theft and report writing. The platform also wrote Japanese forms and fake login pages, and it throttled traffic so each target saw little of it. In a short period in October it ran validation against at least 19 identifiable organisations, at least 16 of them in Japan, plus targets in Taiwan and Hong Kong. Each got a report in the same format. Deep compromise was a very small proportion. For many targets the platform itself recorded no session, no web shell and no exfiltration. The clearest intrusion started at an unauthenticated admin page on an old web system, not a new flaw. A second, human-led case in August and September scanned at least 6,000 Japanese IP addresses over about 24 days and also went after AI and GPU services. A third, from January to October, showed AI-like writing in its scripts, which TrendAI rates as high confidence rather than confirmed, and listed at least 1,300 WebLogic candidates and at least 35 VPN entry points. TrendAI says all of these figures are lower bounds.
stories.matters: One operator with an agent tool can knock on many doors at once, quietly. The doors in this report were still the old ones: exposed admin pages, default passwords and leftover VPN credentials.
stories.imply: An “AI attack” headline is not a count of breaches. Ask what was actually entered. The useful work is still finding the systems you did not mean to leave on the internet.
uses: List public admin pages, old web apps and VPN devices, and close or patch the ones that should not be reachable.
Check edge devices for passwords left in configuration files, not only for new vulnerabilities.
When a report cites an AI attack, separate attempts from confirmed access before you brief the board.
stories.example: A security lead reads the report and spends the week on three checks: admin pages open to the internet, default logins on older web apps, and VPN configs that still contain reusable passwords.
stories.audience: Security teams, IT leads at smaller firms and public bodies, and anyone briefing leadership on AI-driven attacks.
stories.watch: Whether TrendAI names indicators to block. Whether CyberStrikeAI’s maintainers restrict the tool. How often the same pattern shows up outside Japan.

source.title: TrendAI: Not Only ARTEX: The Different Levels AI is Used in Attacks Targeting Japan, 27 October 2026
source.quote: An attempted attack must be distinguished from a compromise.

stories.theme: Nvidia is putting $3 billion into Meta’s share sale and AMD $1 billion, $4 billion in all
stories.changed: On Tuesday 27 October 2026 Nvidia said it will invest $3 billion in Meta’s equity offering, and AMD said it will invest $1 billion. CNBC reports the two together as $4 billion. This follows Meta’s announcement on Monday, covered in Briefing 32, of a plan to raise $95 billion for AI infrastructure: $35 billion in underwritten share sales and a further $60 billion sold gradually on the market. Monday’s announcement said Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom were interested in buying up to $5 billion of shares between them. Tuesday’s statements name Nvidia’s and AMD’s amounts; they do not state Broadcom’s. Nvidia said Meta will expand its use of Vera Rubin chips and Vera CPUs, and that the two will do more work together on Muse, Meta’s assistant. AMD said its Helios racks are running at Meta and its EPYC processors power Muse. CNBC says AMD’s shares rose 3% on Tuesday, Nvidia was flat and Meta fell 1%.
stories.matters: The companies selling Meta its chips are also buying Meta’s new shares. Part of the money raised for AI capacity goes back to the suppliers.
stories.imply: A supplier’s stake is not proof that demand is broader than the deal itself. When you read an AI spending figure, check who is on both sides of it.
uses: If you hold Meta, Nvidia or AMD, note that the chipmakers are financing a customer, which can muddy the demand signal.
In a vendor pitch that cites Meta’s build-out, ask whether the vendor is also buying the customer’s shares.
Do not treat Broadcom as committed to a set amount. Tuesday’s announcements did not name one.
stories.example: A fund analyst updates her note: Nvidia $3 billion and AMD $1 billion are now stated, against Monday’s “up to $5 billion” that also named Broadcom. She leaves Broadcom’s line blank.
stories.audience: Investors, finance teams and anyone reading AI spending as a demand forecast.
stories.watch: Whether Broadcom states an amount. The pricing of Meta’s share sale. Whether other chip buyers take supplier money on the same terms.

source.title: CNBC: Nvidia, AMD to invest $4 billion in Meta as tech giants deepen AI partnership, 27 October 2026
source.quote: Nvidia on Tuesday said it would invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering, with AMD announcing it would invest $1 billion.

stories.theme: A report says the UK Home Office is embedding AI across immigration in near-total secrecy
stories.changed: On 27 October 2026 The Guardian reported a new Open Rights Group study, Automated Discrimination: Unpacking the Digital Hostile Environment. The group says AI now sits across Home Office work and that officials routinely cite national security to refuse freedom-of-information requests. The uses it describes include spotting possible sham marriages, estimating the age of people seeking asylum, checking phones of new arrivals, live facial recognition, and drones and satellites at the border. AI is also used to summarise asylum interviews and the country-policy information used in them, and to prioritise cases through a tool called Identify and Prioritise Immigration Cases. The group wants AI regulated, a ban on uses that risk people’s rights, including ChatGPT tools in asylum applications, a public register of government AI tools, and tighter limits on the national security excuse. A Home Office spokesperson told The Guardian that AI does not replace human decision-makers, that trained caseworkers make asylum decisions, and that the tools only help staff navigate interview records and policy information. They cannot be used on their own and do not decide claims. The department says it monitors the tools and has committed to publishing updated evaluations.
stories.matters: Summaries and priority scores can shape a decision even when a person signs it. People subject to those systems are not being told, the report says, and the paperwork is hard to get.
stories.imply: If you sell AI to a government, or you run one, “a human decides” is not an answer unless you can show what the model drafted and who checked it. Secrecy is now the argument against the system, not only the error rate.
uses: If a model drafts or ranks a decision about a person, record that fact and let the person see the draft.
Publish the tool on the register you already have, and do not answer a disclosure request with a blanket security claim.
Suppliers: keep the evaluation the buyer can publish, including where the tool was wrong.
stories.example: A team bidding to summarise case files for a public body writes into the contract that staff see the summary beside the source text, that the person affected can request it, and that the system is listed on the public AI register.
stories.audience: Public-sector IT and legal teams, govtech suppliers, and anyone whose product drafts a decision about a person.
stories.watch: Whether the Home Office publishes the evaluations it promised. Whether the inspector of borders opens a formal probe. Whether ministers accept a public register.

source.title: The Guardian: ‘Digital hostile environment’: AI secretly being embedded across Home Office, report claims, 27 October 2026
source.quote: Migration is a human phenomenon and experience, not a technical problem that can be fixed by artificial intelligence.

stories.theme: Anthropic published a proof that a famous computing conjecture is false, and says it does not speed up real problems
stories.changed: On 27 October 2026 Anthropic added a paper and a Lean 4 proof to its public formal-math repository: a deterministic algorithm that, it says, solves 3-SAT in time that grows slower than any fixed exponential, which would refute the Exponential Time Hypothesis. The same write-up says the algorithm counts solutions, not only yes or no, in time 2 to the power of O(n log log n over the square root of log n). It says the result was discovered by an internal Claude research model, that the folder is a research artifact, and that the result is purely asymptotic and says nothing about solving formulas in practice. This follows OpenAI’s post on 26 October, which was not in Briefing 32. OpenAI said its own models found a natural-language disproof of the same hypothesis on 16 October and a Lean formalisation on 17 October, and that a group led by Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi and Ryan Williams will examine it. OpenAI says finding usable algorithms, and turning the theory into a practical speed-up, will take significant further research. The same OpenAI post also described a mathematics proof and a physics existence proof; the physics materials are being held for an outside group to write up.
stories.matters: A lab saying a foundational assumption has fallen will show up in strategy decks. The authors of the new paper say it does not make today’s hard problems faster.
stories.imply: Do not change a production system, a security assumption or a research plan because a model produced a proof. Wait until people who did not write it have checked it, and read the sentence about practice.
uses: If someone cites this result in a roadmap, ask them to quote the line that it says nothing about solving real formulas.
Keep scheduling, search and cryptography work on the algorithms you have measured. This paper does not replace them.
If your team uses AI to draft proofs, copy Anthropic’s habit: publish the proof, say what was checked by machine, and say what it does not do.
stories.example: A research lead is asked to brief the board on “AI disproved a core limit.” She sends the Anthropic note that the result is asymptotic, names the outside group looking at OpenAI’s version, and recommends no change to the product.
stories.audience: Research leads, CTOs, and anyone asked to act on an AI-produced scientific claim.
stories.watch: What Impagliazzo, Paturi and Williams report. Whether the two proofs are the same result. Any claim of a speed-up on problems people actually run.

source.title: Anthropic: A 2^o(n) Time Algorithm for 3-SAT, formal-math repository, commit 27 October 2026
source.quote: The result is purely asymptotic and says nothing about solving formulas in practice.

stories.theme: Apple is putting AI assistants, and outside agents, inside Pages, Keynote and Numbers
stories.changed: On Tuesday 27 October 2026 Apple said Creator Studio updates coming to the App Store in November add an intelligent assistant, in beta, to Keynote, Pages and Numbers. It is built on Apple’s models and OpenAI’s, and it uses the document in front of you: designing and animating slides, drafting and restructuring text, and calculating, charting and building tables. The assistant needs an Apple Intelligence device on iOS 27, iPadOS 27 or macOS 27 or later, and it is US English only. The same apps gain Model Context Protocol support on macOS 27 or later, so an outside AI agent can read the file, edit it and run actions. The update is free for existing Creator Studio subscribers. New subscribers pay $12.99 a month or $129 a year in the US. Apple says the free versions of Keynote, Pages and Numbers continue. Keynote also gets an open JSON bundle format, .keyx, meant to be readable by other tools and agents.
stories.matters: The documents many offices already use can now be edited by an assistant, and, on a Mac, by an outside agent. That is useful, and it is a new place for a company file to be read.
stories.imply: Turn on the assistant for a draft you would have written anyway. Before you enable outside agents, decide which documents they may open.
uses: Try the assistant on a draft deck or a first pass of a memo, then edit it yourself. It is a beta, and only in US English.
If you administer Macs, decide whether MCP access to Pages, Keynote and Numbers is allowed, and for which files.
Keep the free apps if you do not want the subscription. The assistant is part of Creator Studio.
stories.example: A communications lead drafts a board update in Pages with the assistant, checks every figure, and asks IT to leave MCP off on machines that hold customer spreadsheets in Numbers.
stories.audience: Anyone who writes in Pages, Keynote or Numbers, and the IT admins who allow agents on Macs.
stories.watch: When it leaves beta and US English. What admins can block. Whether Microsoft and Google match the outside-agent access.

source.title: Apple Newsroom: Apple Creator Studio adds powerful new AI features and even more creative tools, 27 October 2026
source.quote: The assistant understands document context to help users accomplish more without leaving their work.

signals.raw: CNBC 27 Oct: Amazon posted an engineering memo (circulated in September) calling token use, AI adoption and code throughput deeply flawed as targets; 10th and 90th percentile check; no token cap; May leaderboard shut after tokenmaxxing; Brooker cites feature velocity

DeepMind 27 Oct: Genie 4 research preview; first real-time world model with native audio; live text steering; Gemini 3.8 Flash as guiding agent; SynthID on video and audio; trusted testers, then AI Ultra and Gemini API early access; object permanence can drift

TrendAI English report 27 Oct (Japanese 23 Oct): CyberStrikeAI, 44 agents, at least 19 organisations including at least 16 in Japan; many targets recorded no session, no web shell, no exfiltration; lower bounds; second case at least 6,000 Japanese IPs over about 24 days; third case at least 1,300 WebLogic candidates and at least 35 VPN entry points

CNBC 27 Oct: Nvidia to invest $3 billion in Meta’s equity offering, AMD $1 billion, $4 billion total; Monday plan was $95 billion with up to $5 billion of interest from Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom; Vera Rubin, Vera CPU, Muse, Helios, EPYC; AMD +3%, Nvidia flat, Meta -1%

Guardian 27 Oct: ORG report says Home Office AI covers sham marriages, age estimation, phone checks, facial recognition, drones, asylum summaries and Ipic, with FOI blocked; Home Office says caseworkers decide and tools only assist

Anthropic formal-math commit 27 Oct: 3-SAT in 2^o(n), counting in 2^O(n log log n / sqrt(log n)); purely asymptotic, nothing about practice; internal Claude model. OpenAI 26 Oct: disproof found 16 Oct, Lean 17 Oct; Impagliazzo, Paturi and Williams to examine; practical speed-up needs more research
